instruction: In the repository at /luxon (a JavaScript library, luxon, using jest for tests), run the full test suite from the /luxon directory and report the results. Use the command: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 120`. Report: the total number of test suites and tests, the number of failing tests, and the exact names (full test names and file paths) of every failing test. Also report whether the command exited successfully. Do not modify any files. This is a baseline run before any edits.

In the repository /luxon (JavaScript, luxon date library), investigate a bug report and DO NOT FIX IT YET — just diagnose and report. Report only; make no edits.

Bug report: "There is a bug in src/impl/util.js. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` should pass."

Your job:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js fully, and /luxon/src/datetime.js functions `adjustTime`, `plus`, `clone`, `objToLocalTS` usage, and /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js.
2. Look at /luxon/test/datetime/math.test.js (and any other test files) for existing tests mentioning year 100, the "100 barrier", February, or `plus` across year boundaries. Quote them.
3. Run `git -C /luxon log --oneline -5` and `git -C /luxon diff HEAD --stat` and `git -C /luxon show --stat HEAD` to see the repo state. Also check whether the working tree differs from HEAD (`git -C /luxon status --porcelain`).
4. Write a small repro script (e.g. /tmp/repro100.js, or /luxon/tmp_repro100.js which you must delete afterwards) using `import { DateTime } from "/luxon/src/luxon.js";` run via `cd /luxon && npx babel-node <file>`, that prints results for cases like:
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 12, day: 31}).plus({days: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({days: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({months: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 2, day: 28}).plus({days: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 2, day: 28}).plus({days: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 1, day: 1}).plus({months: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 3, day: 1}).minus({months: 1}).toISO()
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 2, day: 28}).plus({days: 1}).toISODate(), and the same with year 2000, 4, 0, 1
   - DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 2, day: 28}).plus({days: 1}).toUTC().toISO()
   - Also DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 2, day: 28}).plus({days: 1}).valueOf() vs new Date(Date.UTC(100,2,1)).valueOf()
   Include also the analogous cases for year 99 and year 101 for comparison, and print `DateTime.fromObject({year:100,month:1,day:31}).plus({months:1}).day`.
   IMPORTANT: run these with the default zone set to UTC (`Settings.defaultZoneName = "utc"`) and also with the local zone, and report both.
5. Compare the behavior for years < 100 vs >= 100 and identify precisely which line in src/impl/util.js is wrong, and what the correct code should be. Explain the mechanism (e.g. Date.UTC mapping years 0-99 to 1900-1999, and how the revert logic interacts with leap-year/February calculations).
6. Also check whether the same bug affects `daysInMonth`, `isLeapYear`, `weeksInWeekYear`, `untruncateYear`, `parseMillis`, `roundTo`, `floorMod`, `padStart`, `signedOffset`, `formatOffset` — i.e. verify each function in util.js against its documented/intended behavior by writing small checks, and report any OTHER discrepancy you find in util.js (with evidence).

Report: the exact wrong line(s), the mechanism, the proposed minimal fix, the repro output, and any other util.js discrepancies found. Do not edit any repository file.

You are working in the JavaScript repository /luxon (the luxon date library, tests via jest). Your job: reproduce, fix and verify ONE bug in /luxon/src/datetime.js. Do not modify any other source file, and never modify or delete any file under /luxon/test.

THE BUG REPORT: "There is a bug in src/datetime.js. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th` should pass." In 1974 the USA observed daylight saving time from January 6th through October 27th (year-round DST), so for zone America/New_York every DateTime from 1974-01-06 to 1974-10-27 must have `isInDST === true`, and dates outside that window (1974-01-01..01-05, 1974-10-28..12-31) must have `isInDST === false`.

STEP 1 - REPRODUCE. Write a temp script /luxon/tmp_dst_check.js (delete it at the end) that imports `import { DateTime, Settings } from "./src/luxon.js";`, sets `Settings.defaultZoneName = "America/New_York"`, and prints `isInDST` plus `offset` for every day from 1974-01-01 to 1974-12-31 (and also 1974-01-06T12:00, 1974-10-27T12:00, 1974-10-28T12:00). Run it with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node tmp_dst_check.js`. Also print `DateTime.fromObject({year:1974,month:1,day:15}).offset` and `DateTime.fromObject({year:1974,month:1,day:1}).offset` to confirm the container's tzdata really has the 1974 US rule (offsets -240 for DST, -300 for EST). Report the raw output. Identify exactly which dates are wrong.

STEP 2 - DIAGNOSE. Read the `isInDST` getter in /luxon/src/datetime.js (around line 1164) and explain why the wrong dates are wrong. (Expected diagnosis: it compares `this.offset` with `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset`; when the DateTime is already in January, `set({ month: 1 })` returns the same instant, so the January reference offset is the DST offset itself and the comparison is false. The reference must be a date guaranteed to be in standard time, i.e. January 1st.)

STEP 3 - FIX. Apply the minimal fix in the `isInDST` getter: change `this.set({ month: 1 })` to `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })`. Change nothing else. Keep prettier formatting (2-space indent, double quotes) and keep the JSDoc comment.

STEP 4 - VERIFY (report all raw output):
 a) Re-run the temp script: every day 1974-01-06..1974-10-27 must print isInDST true, and every day 1974-01-01..1974-01-05 and 1974-10-28..1974-12-31 must print false. Print a summary line `MISMATCHES: <n>` and make it 0.
 b) Also verify these still behave correctly (print results): America/Los_Angeles 2016-01-15 -> false, 2016-05-15 -> true, 2016-12-15 -> false; Australia/Sydney 2016-01-15 -> true, 2016-07-15 -> false; a fixed-offset zone e.g. DateTime.fromObject({year:2016,month:5,day:1},{zone:"UTC+3"}).isInDST -> false; DateTime.invalid("because").isInDST -> falsy; and a southern-hemisphere zone in 1974 is not required.
 c) Run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime 2>&1 | tail -n 30` and `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 30`. Report pass/fail counts and the names of ALL failing tests. NOTE: there are 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding: `DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds`) - these are unrelated and must remain the ONLY failures.
 d) Run `git -C /luxon diff src/datetime.js` and report the exact diff. Run `git -C /luxon status --porcelain` and confirm only src/datetime.js is modified (plus temp files, which you must delete). Delete /luxon/tmp_dst_check.js.

Report: the diagnosis, the exact diff, the verification outputs (including the mismatch count), and the full list of failing tests.

You are working in the JavaScript repository /luxon (the luxon date library, tests via jest). Your job: fix ONE bug in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js and verify it. Do NOT modify any other file. NEVER modify or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do NOT touch untracked scratch files/dirs created by other agents (e.g. /luxon/tmp_*.js, /luxon/tmp_fixed_src) except the temp file you create yourself.

THE BUG REPORT: "There is a bug in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js. Once it is fixed, the tests `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset` should pass."

CURRENT CODE (whole file, /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js): the class extends Zone, has a constructor storing `this.fixed = offset`, and `get isValid() { return true; }`. So `new FixedOffsetZone("bogus").isValid` is `true`, and `DateTime.fromObject({year: 2017}, {zone: new FixedOffsetZone("bogus")})` / `DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone: new FixedOffsetZone("bogus")})` are NOT invalid even though the zone is garbage. The DateTime constructor marks a DateTime invalid when `!zone.isValid` (see src/datetime.js constructor, `(!zone.isValid ? unsupportedZone(zone) : null)`), so the zone must report invalidity.

THE FIX: change the `isValid` getter to
```js
  /** @override **/
  get isValid() {
    return isNumber(this.fixed);
  }
```
and add the needed import at the top of the file: change `import { formatOffset, signedOffset } from "../impl/util.js";` to `import { formatOffset, signedOffset, isNumber } from "../impl/util.js";`. Change NOTHING else (keep the JSDoc comments, 2-space indentation, double quotes). Do not add validation to the constructor or to `instance()`.

VERIFICATION (report all raw output):
1. Write a temp script /luxon/tmp_foz_check.js (delete it at the end) that imports `import { DateTime, FixedOffsetZone, Settings } from "./src/luxon.js";` and prints/asserts:
   - `FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance.isValid === true`
   - `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60).isValid === true`
   - `new FixedOffsetZone("bogus").isValid === false`
   - `new FixedOffsetZone(undefined).isValid === false`
   - `new FixedOffsetZone(null).isValid === false`
   - `new FixedOffsetZone(NaN).isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("bogus") }).isValid === false` and print its `invalidReason` (expect "unsupported zone")
   - `DateTime.fromObject({ year: 2017, month: 5, day: 25 }, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("bogus") }).isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.fromISO("2017-05-25", { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("bogus") }).isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.local().setZone(new FixedOffsetZone("bogus")).isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance(60) }).isValid === true` and `DateTime.utc().isValid === true`
   - `DateTime.fromObject({year:2017,month:5,day:25},{zone:"UTC+3"}).isValid === true` and its `zoneName` is "UTC+3"
   Print `FAILURES: <n>` and make it 0. Run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node tmp_foz_check.js`.
2. Run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones test/datetime 2>&1 | tail -n 30` and `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 30`. Report pass/fail counts and the names of ALL failing tests. NOTE: exactly 2 pre-existing failures are expected and allowed, both in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding): `DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds`. Any OTHER failure means something broke: report it and investigate.
3. Run `git -C /luxon diff src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` and report the exact diff. Run `git -C /luxon status --porcelain` and confirm src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js is modified and that NO file under test/ is modified (other modified src files from other agents are expected). Delete /luxon/tmp_foz_check.js.

Report: the exact diff, the verification output (including FAILURES count), the jest results,

You are working in the JavaScript repository /luxon (the luxon date library, tests via jest). URGENT single bug fix in /luxon/src/duration.js, then verification. Do not modify any other source file, and never modify or delete anything under /luxon/test.

THE BUG REPORT: "There is a bug in src/duration.js. Once it is fixed, the test `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` should pass." The expected behavior is that converting/normalizing between ANY pair of units works, i.e. for every pair of units (years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) the conversion factor exists.

SUSPECTED ROOT CAUSE: in the `casualMatrix` object near the top of /luxon/src/duration.js, the `quarters` entry is missing the `seconds` conversion factor (it has months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, milliseconds but NOT seconds), so `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize()` yields NaN, and `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1}).shiftTo("seconds")` also yields NaN. The `accurateMatrix.quarters` entry DOES have seconds, and `casualMatrix.years`/`casualMatrix.months` both have seconds, so `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds` is the odd one out.

STEP 1 - REPRODUCE. Write a temp script /luxon/tmp_dur_check.js (delete it at the end) that imports `import { Duration } from "./src/luxon.js";` and:
 a) prints `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1}).shiftTo("seconds").toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}).as("seconds")`;
 b) systematically loops over ALL ordered unit pairs [years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds] and for each ordered pair (a,b) with a !== b builds `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1 }).normalize()` and checks that NO value in the resulting object is NaN, printing every failing pair. Do the same for `.shiftTo(b)` and for `.as(b)`. Print `FAILING PAIRS: <n>` for each check.
 Run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node tmp_dur_check.js`. Report the raw output and the exact list of failing pairs.

STEP 2 - FIX. Add the missing `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` entry to the `quarters` object of `casualMatrix` in /luxon/src/duration.js, placed in the same position/order as in the `years` and `months` entries (i.e. after `minutes` and before `milliseconds`). Change NOTHING else. Keep prettier formatting (2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas as in the surrounding code).

STEP 3 - VERIFY (report all raw output):
 a) Re-run the temp script: all three checks must report 0 failing pairs. Also print `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("seconds")` (should be 7862400) and `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 4}).as("years")` (should be 1).
 b) Run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -n 30` and `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 30`. Report pass/fail counts and the names of ALL failing tests. NOTE: there are 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding: `DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds`) - these are unrelated and must remain the ONLY failures.
 c) Also confirm the accurate matrix path still works: `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}, {conversionAccuracy: "longterm"}).normalize().toObject()` must have no NaN.
 d) Run `git -C /luxon diff src/duration.js` and report the exact diff. Run `git -C /luxon status --porcelain` and confirm only src/duration.js is modified (plus your temp file, which you must delete). Delete /luxon/tmp_dur_check.js.

Report: the exact diff, the reproduction output before the fix, the verification output after the fix (including failing-pair counts), and the full list of failing tests.
